rules.rule: POST /payments/webhook requires the raw (unparsed) request body and a valid stripe-signature header verified via stripe.webhooks.constructEvent against STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET; an invalid/unverifiable signature returns 400 and is logged at warn.

Webhook deliveries are deduped by Stripe event id via an atomic upsert into WebhookEvent; a delivery already 'processed' is skipped without re-running business logic. A 'failed' or fresh 'received' row is NOT skipped — Stripe's own retry is expected to reach this path again.
Any thrown error from an event handler marks the WebhookEvent 'failed' and rethrows, reaching AllExceptionsFilter as a 500 — the intended signal for Stripe to retry.

payment_intent.succeeded with no matching Order throws deliberately (treated as a timing race between Stripe's confirmation and the Order row becoming queryable) so Stripe retries until the Order exists.

payment_intent.payment_failed / payment_intent.canceled with no matching Order is a silent no-op (warn + return, never throws) — this is the expected, permanent case for a declined/withdrawn/expired/superseded offer-hold PaymentIntent, which never had an Order.
A mismatch between the webhook's captured amount and Order.total is logged at error but does not block recording the payment as succeeded, since the charge already happened on Stripe's side.

charge.refunded is a no-op if Payment.status is already 'refunded'; otherwise full-vs-partial is derived from the cumulative Charge.amount_refunded vs Payment.amount, and any tax-transaction reversal is sized to the increment over the previously-recorded cumulative total, not the running total itself.

charge.dispute.* and transfer.* events are platform-account events dispatched into ConnectService rather than handled in this module; a missing ConnectService wiring logs at error (not silent) though the webhook delivery still resolves 200.
rules.note: Dispute/chargeback business logic itself is owned by connect/orders-disputes modules — not re-derived here.

rules.rule: refundOrderPayment only acts on a Payment in 'succeeded' or 'partially_refunded' status, caps the refund to the remaining unrefunded balance, and maps Stripe client-caused failures (e.g. already charged back) to 400 while rethrowing anything else as a genuine 500.

Every retryable Stripe-side write in this module (customer/account creation, transfer, refund, tax transaction/reversal) carries an idempotencyKey scoped to the specific operation and order/event, so a network retry of the same call cannot duplicate its real-world effect.

A sibling raw-body route, /payments/webhook/connect, exists under ConnectModule and shares the same WebhookEvent dedup table — out of this module's 6-endpoint scope but relevant to understanding the full Stripe webhook surface.
rules.note: Boundary note only — not analyzed further here.

rules.rule: All three endpoints (GET/POST/DELETE) require JwtAuthGuard at the controller class level — there are no public routes in this module.

Attach is idempotent two ways: (a) the exact Stripe PaymentMethod id already saved for the user returns that row with alreadySaved:true and makes no Stripe call; (b) a different id but the same physical card (brand+last4+expMonth+expYear) already saved returns the existing row with alreadySaved:true and detaches the newly-created Stripe clone.
Only visa/mastercard/amex/discover may be saved; any other brand is attached (to learn its brand from Stripe), then detached again and rejected with 400.
A stale/cross-environment stripeCustomerId (Stripe 'resource_missing' with param 'customer') triggers exactly one auto-recreate-and-retry of the Stripe customer before failing.
Delete is ownership-checked (403 if not the caller's row) and blocked with 409 if the card currently backs an open (pending/countered, unexpired) offer hold, checked before any Stripe call.

Delete is a hard delete at both Stripe (tolerant of an already-detached PaymentMethod) and the local DB row — no soft delete. Orders/Offers never hold a live FK to PaymentMethod for history; they snapshot cardBrand/cardLast4 at creation time, so a later deletion never corrupts a past order/offer record.

PaymentMethod.isDefault exists in the schema and response DTO and drives findAll's sort order, but no code path anywhere sets it to true — there is no set-default endpoint. In practice findAll is always sorted newest-first.
rules.note: Dead field, not a bug — nothing is broken, the sort key is simply a no-op in practice.

rules.rule: The idempotency checks in attach() (exact-id and same-card) are application-level findFirst reads with no backing DB unique constraint, so two concurrent identical POST requests can both pass the check and insert two rows. Confirmed as a live, currently-open issue — REDB1-39/BRI-434 — where this exact application-level fix is verified live yet duplicate rows pre-exist in the shared DB and were never cleaned up pending sign-off.

A PaymentMethod row detached from Stripe out-of-band (Dashboard or expiry) is never revalidated by this module — GET keeps listing it, attach/delete don't re-check it. The failure only surfaces downstream at checkout as a raw, uncaught Stripe error.
rules.note: Fix boundary is orders.service.ts, not this module — flagged here because the stale-row condition originates in this module's data.

rules.rule: GET /shipping/tiers is public (no guard) by design, so mobile/web can show it before a user is confirmed as a seller.
The 4 shipping-fee tiers are hard-coded application constants, not DB-driven or admin-configurable. A prior ShippingConfig table/service existed and was deliberately removed.

Tier prices/weight bands are the single source of truth also consumed by ai/shippability.ts's weight-to-tier suggestion logic and by mobile+web frontends — must not be independently re-declared anywhere.

POST /shipping/webhook/shippo is a pure no-op unless SHIPPO_TRACKING_MODE=webhook is explicitly configured; polling is the documented production default/authoritative tracking source, and this route does not perform signature verification at all when tracking mode is not 'webhook'.

When webhook mode is active, HMAC (header shippo-auth-signature, t=/v1= format, SHA-256 over '<timestamp>.<rawBody>', constant-time compare) takes precedence over a URL ?token= shared secret; at least one must be configured or boot fails.

If neither HMAC secret nor URL token is configured, the handler falls open (warns, accepts unauthenticated) rather than rejecting — reachable in practice only by a local dev boot that bypasses env validation, since normal boot refuses to start in that combination.

The webhook resolves 200 for every safe-to-ignore case (tracking mode off, non-track_updated event, unknown carrier+tracking pair) so Shippo stops retrying those; it throws 400/401 for a payload/auth problem Shippo should not retry, and lets a genuine unexpected error propagate to a 500 that Shippo WILL retry.

(carrier, trackingNumber) has no DB-level uniqueness on Shipment; a webhook matching more than one row resolves to the most-recently-created one, logged at error for manual investigation rather than failing the request.

Inbound webhook field names are read defensively in both snake_case and camelCase because the exact wire payload shape has never been confirmed against a real Shippo delivery (only documented, per the BRI-257 POC's own finding that it never received one).

A valid, resolvable tracking update emits a 'shippo.tracking-updated' event via EventEmitter2 rather than calling OrdersService/DisputesService directly, specifically to avoid a forwardRef module cycle. The actual status-transition logic those services apply is out of this module's scope.
rules.note: Cross-reference orders-disputes agent's output for the consuming side.

rules.rule: Shipment.labelUrl/qrCodeUrl store long-lived (~1 year), unauthenticated Shippo bearer links containing shipping PII. The endpoint returning them to a seller is outside this module's 6-endpoint scope, but the data originates in this module's Shipment model.
rules.note: Flagged as a boundary-relevant security gap, not fixable within this module's own endpoints.
